Name: The Longest Year
Author: sonofskywalker3
Description:
[size=6][b]The Longest Year[/b][/size]
[size=4][b]Restore the Community Center within a single year — or the Junimos rewind the seasons and you begin again, a little stronger.[/b][/size]

A roguelite time-loop for Stardew Valley (PC).

[b]The Longest Year[/b] turns Stardew Valley's first year into a roguelite loop. Each season asks you to give back enough of the land's bounty to the old Community Center hall. Fall short by a season's end and the Junimos turn time back to Spring 1 — the world resets, but the strength you've earned (and the power your offerings bank) can carry forward. Restore the whole Center inside one year to break the loop for good.

[color=yellow][b]Version 1.1.[/b] The full first year, story and all. Bug reports and balance feedback are still very welcome; see Giving feedback below.[/color]

[size=5][b]What's New in 1.1.8[/b][/size]

[b]Fixed: day 2 would not save after a rewind with Farm Type Manager packs.[/b] The save right after the rewind made the game announce a second morning, so Farm Type Manager spawned its monsters twice and lost track of some. A ghost it forgot stayed in the world and stopped the next night's save. The rewind's save no longer counts as a new morning. Thanks to SylviaStormsinger for the report and the log.

[b]Fixed: bundles no longer count on a Desert Festival stall that may never open.[/b] Each festival day picks two villagers at random to run a stall, so an item only one villager's stall sells or trades (Pierre's Squid, Leah's Hardwood) is luck, not something the board can expect you to get. The Egg Shop still counts, since it opens every day. Thanks to SylviaStormsinger.

[b]Fixed: "To The Beach" no longer stays in your quest log when you already have a rod.[/b] Keeping your fishing rod through the rewind, or buying it as a focus card, skips Willy's beach scene so he doesn't hand you a second pole. That scene was also what closed his quest. Walking onto the beach now closes it. Thanks to tanky24u.

[b]Fixed: Qi gems and Casino coins now rewind with your gold.[/b] Both stayed in your wallet through the rewind. Thanks to sarahwinchester97.

[size=5][b]1.1.4[/b][/size]

[b]Fixed: a settings tooltip named the wrong stall.[/b] The Starting cart slots setting's tooltip said the cart stays empty on Hard and Extreme until you buy Cart Stall I. The first stall upgrade is Cart Stall II, and the tooltip now says so.

[size=5][b]1.1.3[/b][/size]

[b]Changed: loading a save is faster.[/b] The base game's item routes now ship with the mod instead of being worked out on every load, which took several seconds. Nothing about how a board is built changed. If your mods change the game's data, TLY still works the routes out itself once and remembers them. Supported mods will get their own shipped answers over time.

[b]Changed: shipped item routes are tied to the mod version.[/b] The routes that ship with the mod are only used by the TLY version they were made for. If the file and the mod ever disagree, TLY works the routes out itself once and remembers them, so an out-of-date file can never give a wrong board.

[size=5][b]1.0.27[/b][/size]

[b]New: the Traveling Cart brings Year 2 items.[/b] Every cart visit has a 1 in 10 chance that one of its slots holds something a loop normally can't get before the Community Center is done: Garlic, Red Cabbage and Artichoke Seeds, Ginger Island crops and fish, Mr. Qi's goods, dishes whose recipe only airs in Year 2, and the same kinds of late-game items from your other mods. It is one chance per visit however many cart slots you have bought, and it only offers the kinds of things the cart already sells. Thanks to mysticalfairy25 for the idea.

[b]Fixed: the cart's special items show up again.[/b] Rare Seed, Coffee Beans, the catalogues and the cart's other fixed items came after its random stock, so with TLY's cart slots they never made it onto the cart. Each one now takes a random slot like any other item. On the day the cart's guaranteed Red Cabbage Seeds visit comes up, the seeds always get a slot.

Older changes: see the [url=https://github.com/sonofskywalker3/TheLongestYear/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md]changelog[/url].

[size=5][b]Features[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]Seasonal time-loop.[/b] Each season has a donation minimum. Miss it and the year unwinds to Spring 1.[/*]
[*][b]Junimo Points.[/b] Donations earn JP — scaled by rarity and by how late in the year you give. JP banks across loops.[/*]
[*][b]Junimo Upgrades.[/b] Spend JP on upgrades that let you hold on to some of what you gained: skill levels, tool tiers (the trash can too), recipes, buildings, a kept pet, the power books you have read, your wallet items and Stardrops, the Junimos' own gifts (greenhouse, quarry bridge, boulder, minecarts, bus), Pierre selling his year-two seeds in year one, and more.[/*]
[*][b]Focus cards.[/b] At the start of each loop, pick one card from each of three hands: tools, buildings and knacks. Buy a picked card with JP any time that year, the Junimos deliver it, and you keep it for later loops.[/*]
[*][b]Animal powers.[/b] The upgrade menu's [b]Animals[/b] tab sells permanent animal upgrades. None of them makes a bundle ask for more. Your animal keeps (Keep Horse, Keep Pet, Keep Coop, Keep Barn, Keep Silo, the Start with animals and the Herd Book) live on the same tab.
[list]
[*][b]Morning Rounds:[/b] every animal on your farm gets petted each morning, like an Auto-Petter.[/*]
[*][b]Warm Welcome I, II and III:[/b] new animals arrive with 1, 2 or 3 hearts. Animals coming back from the Herd Book keep their own hearts.[/*]
[*][b]Quick Growth:[/b] a baby animal grows up after its first night with food.[/*]
[*][b]Fast Hatch:[/b] eggs in an incubator hatch in half the time.[/*]
[*][b]Growing Herd:[/b] cows, goats, sheep and pigs give birth about four times as often. Shows up once you've had a Big Barn.[/*]
[*][b]Snug Barn:[/b] your animals stay happy on rainy and Winter days they spend indoors.[/*]
[*][b]Busy Coop:[/b] ducks lay every day and rabbits every 2 days.[/*]
[*][b]Busy Barn:[/b] goats and sheep produce every day.[/*]
[*][b]Molting Season:[/b] ducks have an extra 25% chance to leave a Duck Feather instead of an egg. Shows up once you've owned a duck.[/*]
[*][b]Lucky Rabbits:[/b] rabbits always leave a Rabbit's Foot instead of Wool. Shows up once you've owned a rabbit.[/*]
[*][b]Truffle Hog:[/b] each truffle a pig digs up has a 25% chance to be two. Shows up once you've owned a pig.[/*]
[*][b]Swift Horse:[/b] your horse runs about 10% faster. Needs Keep Horse.[/*]
[*][b]Horse Flute:[/b] start every loop with a Horse Flute. Needs Keep Horse.[/*]
[*][b]Loyal Pet:[/b] your pet brings presents twice as often, starting at 3 hearts instead of 5.[/*]
[/list][/*]
[*][b]Gear.[/b] The upgrade menu's [b]Gear[/b] tab has nine chains that give your tools and weapons the effect of a Forge enchantment, no Volcano needed: faster swings, cheaper energy, harder hits, wider charges, a bigger watering can, a steadier fishing line, and weapon damage, speed and defense. Gear that already has the real enchantment gets the better of the two, never both.[/*]
[*][b]Exp Boost.[/b] Exp Boost I to V in the Efficiency tab boosts all five skills at once, up to +150%. Mastery Boost I and II give +50% and double Mastery experience.[/*]
[*][b]JP Boosts.[/b] The Junimo statue on your farm sells this-loop edges for JP: tomorrow's rain or a lucky day, a free late night, stacking forage/fish/crop/mine/drop chances, a faster walk, a season of cheaper shops, faster friendships, extra energy, a skill level on the spot, an elevator stop you have not earned yet, or a week of a past season's fish and forage. An Active tab shows what is running and a Plan tab shows what each keep still needs.[/*]
[*][b]Weekly themes.[/b] Each week, pick one of two themes (Foraging, Farming, Fishing, Mining, Mixed, Spelunking, Artisan, Kitchen) for a bonus and a paired liability. Goals follow the season gate and the weekly bonus is paid per goal. One goal on a theme card can carry an x2 badge: every item you donate to it earns twice the usual JP.[/*]
[*][b]Randomizer.[/b] An optional settings section that adds chance to the weekly themes, goals, bundle rewards and the cart. Everything in it starts off.[/*]
[*][b]Carryover surfaces.[/b] A [b]Bundle Log[/b] book that tracks each season's goals (also a tab on the Collections page, so you can check it from anywhere), a Cookbook and Craftbook to bank recipes, a [b]Herd Book[/b] that brings your registered animals back with their hearts, and a Junimo Stash chest that survives resets.[/*]
[*][b]A story.[/b] Play it to find out.[/*]
[*][b]A starved Traveling Cart.[/b] Joja has squeezed the merchant's suppliers — the cart carries [b]one item[/b] per visit until you unlock more stalls with the [b]Cart Stall[/b] upgrades (and Cart Whisperer previews what's coming). Prefer the full vanilla cart? Turn off [font=Courier New]LimitTravelingCartStock[/font]. Each visit also has a 1 in 10 chance that one slot holds a Year 2 item: Garlic, Red Cabbage or Artichoke Seeds, Ginger Island crops and fish, Mr. Qi's goods, and the like.[/*]
[*][b]The town half-remembers.[/b] Villagers you have spent a lot of time with across loops occasionally say something uncanny. From the second loop, festivals stir it up too. At most festivals one villager half-remembers something you did there in an earlier loop: the egg hunt you won, the dance you shared, what you put in the soup. Talk to people to find out who. Win the egg hunt and someone will bring it up at the next Egg Festival, and everyone you have danced with may remember it when you ask again. No gameplay effect, and it never explains itself. Toggle in Features.[/*]
[*][b]Break the loop.[/b] Finish the Center in a year and the year ends the next morning. Then loop again or keep playing to the end of the year.[/*]
[/list][line]

[list]
[*][b]Stardew Valley 1.6+[/b] (PC: Windows, Linux, macOS)[/*]
[*][b]SMAPI 4.0.0[/b] or newer[/*]

[size=5][b]Install[/b][/size]
[list=1]
[*]Install [url=https://smapi.io/]SMAPI[/url] (4.0.0+).[/*]
[*]Download the latest [font=Courier New]TheLongestYear[/font] release and unzip it into your [font=Courier New]Stardew Valley/Mods[/font] folder, so you have [font=Courier New]Mods/TheLongestYear/TheLongestYear.dll[/font].[/*]
[*]Launch the game through SMAPI.[/*]
[*][b]Start a new game[/b] on any farm type. Leave [b]Skip intro[/b] off the first time: the mod's own opening plays in place of the vanilla one and explains the loop. Tick it on later farms to go straight to the theme picker.[/*]
[*][b]Community Center Bundles[/b] under [b]New → Advanced Options[/b] defaults to [b]TLY Custom[/b]: every loop rolls a fresh board from the vanilla + remix pools plus the mod's own authored bundles, using vanilla items only unless you turn on Allow mod items in custom bundles. Prefer the game's own board (or another bundle mod's)? Pick [b]Normal[/b] or [b]Remixed[/b] there instead. The mod keeps that board and re-rolls it the same way on every reset. With other mods installed, those bundles may not reshuffle each loop and may ask for items you can't get. (You can change this later: [font=Courier New]Bundle source[/font] in GMCM switches an existing save between all three, applying at its next loop.)
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/47192/47192-1787355673-935410882.png[/img][/*]
[/list][line]

[size=5][b]How it works[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]The opening.[/b] A new game starts with the mod's own opening, which explains the loop. You wake on Spring 1 and pick your first [b]weekly theme[/b].[/*]
[*][b]Weekly themes.[/b] Each week you choose one of two offered themes. Room themes (Foraging, Farming, Fishing, Mining) take goals from their Community Center room; Spelunking, Artisan and Kitchen take goals by item kind from anywhere on the board, and Mixed takes anything. Goals follow what the season gate demands first; the weekly JP bonus is paid goal by goal and the drawback lifts when every goal is done. The planning hub opens at the start of each week.[/*]
[*][b]Seasonal goals.[/b] The [b]Bundle Log[/b] book (click to open) tracks each season's required donations. Each season has a minimum you must donate to the Center before the season turns. [b]Miss it and the year unwinds to Spring 1.[/b][/*]
[*][b]Fail night.[/b] When a season's minimum is missed, the Junimos rewind the year. Before the upgrade menu opens, they ask whether to keep the same bundle board for the next loop or let time reshuffle it. The first hold is free; each further hold in a row costs 50, 100, 200, then 300 JP, and reshuffling resets the price. This works on every bundle source.[/*]
[*][b]Junimo Points (JP).[/b] Donations earn JP, scaled by rarity and by how late in the year you give (later seasons are worth much more). JP banks across loops.[/*]
[*][b]Junimo Upgrades.[/b] On every loop reset (and on a win), spend banked JP on upgrades that let you [i]hold on to some of what you gained[/i] next loop — skill levels, tool tiers, recipes, buildings, a kept pet, the power books you have read, your wallet items and Stardrops, and more.[/*]
[*][b]Focus cards.[/b] Before the first planning hub of every loop, the Junimos offer three hands of cards in turn (tools, buildings, knacks) and you pick one from each. Buy a picked card with JP from the farm statue's Focus tab any time that year. The Junimos deliver it then and there, and you keep it for later loops. A card you don't buy stays in the upgrade menu at the end of the year.[/*]
[*][b]JP Boosts.[/b] The Junimo statue on the farm sells this-loop edges for JP any day (weather, luck, a free late night, stacking bonuses, a temporary skill level, an elevator stop) and shows what is running on its Active tab.[/*]
[*][b]Carryover surfaces on the farm.[/b] A [b]Cookbook[/b] (kitchen) and [b]Craftbook[/b] (table) let you bank recipes to keep; a [b]Junimo Stash[/b] chest preserves a few items across resets.[/*]
[*][b]Restarting.[/b] Want a fresh loop before the season runs out? The Junimo Shrine's [b]Restart the year[/b] button ends the day and runs a Fail night without the Junimo scene: keep or reshuffle your bundles, spend JP, bank recipes, and wake on Spring 1. It counts as a loop, and it works after Keep playing too.[/*]
[*][b]Winning.[/b] Restore the entire Community Center within a year to break the loop. The year ends the next morning; then loop again or keep playing to the end of the year.[/*]
[/list][line]

[size=5][b]Difficulty[/b][/size]
Eleven difficulty dials live in the mod's settings menu (GMCM) under [b]Difficulty[/b], with one overall [b]Difficulty[/b] option above them. Pick a level there and every dial switches to it, then change any single dial you like. Every dial has four steps, [b]Easy / Normal / Hard / Extreme[/b], and every one starts on [b]Normal[/b], which is the balance the mod ships with. Changing nothing changes nothing.

[b]Changes take effect on your next loop, not straight away.[/b] The dials are stamped onto your save when a loop begins, so the year you are already playing keeps the rules it started under.
[img]https://staticdelivery.nexusmods.com/mods/1303/images/47192/47192-1787870999-2094236733.png[/img]

[b]What the bundles ask for[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Stack size.[/b] How many of an item a slot asks for, as a share of what a week of going after it actually yields: Easy 10 to 30%, Normal 20 to 50%, Hard 50 to 65%, Extreme 65 to 80%, and never above 80%. Fish, forage, crops, crab pots, monster drops, the mines, animals and machines each have their own yield behind that number, and a yield is capped at one stack of 99 (Slime, Bat Wings and the like), so an Extreme ask of 80 is a stack, not a share. Artifacts stay at one. Money bundles are never affected.[/*]
[*][b]Once-per-loop items ask for one.[/b] On by default. The five legendary fish, the two books hidden around town and the Golden Pumpkin can only be had once in a loop, so a bundle never asks for more than one of them whatever Stack size says. Off, they scale like everything else. Takes effect at the next reset.[/*]
[*][b]Quality asks.[/b] How often a slot wants a silver or gold star. Items the game never gives a star to are still never asked for at quality, at any step.[/*]
[*][b]Required slots.[/b] How many of a bundle's shown items you must actually donate. Hard asks for one more, Easy one fewer, Extreme asks for all of them.[/*]
[*][b]Item rarity.[/b] Weights bundles toward harder items: rarer, later in the year, or needing a keg or a press. [b]TLY Custom bundles only[/b] (see below).[/*]
[*][b]Bundles per room.[/b] How many bundles each Community Center room has. Easy has one or two fewer, never below 2. Normal is the usual count. Hard has one or two more. Extreme fills every room to 9. Extra bundles come from the same pool as the rest and are due in their own season. The Vault changes too: Easy drops its most expensive bundle, Hard adds one at twice that price, and Extreme adds another at 1.6 times the Hard one. The bus is repaired once every Vault bundle on your board is paid, and the season checkpoints never ask for more Vault bundles than your board has. The Missing Bundle never changes. [b]TLY Custom bundles only[/b] (see below).[/*]
[/list][b]What you carry between loops[/b]
[list]
[*][b]Junimo Points earned.[/b] Scales every JP award, so progress across loops is faster or slower. The season ramp keeps its shape, so late-season donating is still worth the most.[/*]
[*][b]Upgrade prices.[/b] Scales what upgrades cost in the upgrade menu.[/*]
[*][b]Starting gold.[/b] Scales the [font=Courier New]StartingMoney[/font] value rather than replacing it. Extreme starts you with nothing.[/*]
[*][b]Starting cart slots.[/b] How many items the Traveling Cart offers before you buy any Cart Stall upgrade. On Hard and Extreme the cart is empty until you buy Cart Stall II.[/*]
[*][b]Hold prices.[/b] Scales the JP price of keeping your board on a Fail night. The first hold stays free at every step.[/*]
[/list][b]Darkness.[/b] How hard the darkness hits from Summer on. The tooltip in the settings menu has the details.

[b]Two dials do not work on vanilla boards.[/b] Item rarity and Bundles per room apply to [b]TLY Custom[/b] bundles only, because changing which item a vanilla bundle asks for, or how many bundles a room has, would be changing the board. Stack size, quality asks and required slots all work on vanilla Standard and Remixed boards too.

[font=Courier New]tly_difficulty[/font] in the SMAPI console prints what your save is actually running under, including anything you have changed since your last loop. Please attach it to any balance report.

[line]

[size=5][b]Switching bundle source later[/b][/size]
You are not locked into the board you picked when you started. [b]Bundle source[/b] in the mod's settings menu (GMCM) is one setting with three choices, and you can move an existing save between any of them:
[list]
[*][b]TLY Custom[/b] - the mod composes a fresh board every loop from the vanilla and remix pools plus its own authored bundles. It asks only for vanilla items and gives only vanilla rewards: other mods' items are left out so the balance holds. [b]Allow mod items in custom bundles[/b], next to Bundle source, lets other mods' items in. It is off on new games, and saves from before 0.19.4 start with it on. Other mods aren't supported, so with it on a bundle may ask for an item you can't get.[/*]
[*][b]Normal[/b] - the game's own standard bundle layout, re-rolled the same way each loop.[/*]
[*][b]Remixed[/b] - the game's own remixed layout, likewise.[/*]
[/list]Another bundle mod's board is covered by Normal or Remixed: whatever the game generates is what the mod keeps. Using Normal or Remixed with other mods (bundle mods included) is allowed, but the bundles may not reshuffle each loop and may ask for items you can't get. With Tech's Cross-Mod Bundles, both Normal and Remixed roll a fresh board each loop.

Like the difficulty dials, a switch applies at your [b]next loop[/b], not straight away. The year you are already playing keeps the board it started with. The setting belongs to the save you have loaded. On the title screen it only picks what a new game starts with, so one farm's choice never changes another's.

[b]Keeping your board on a Fail night works on all three.[/b] If you hold, you get the same board back next loop whichever source it came from.

[size=5][b]Is this a bug?[/b][/size]

A few things get reported often enough to be worth answering up front.

[b]Demetrius never shows up about the cave, I just get a popup asking mushrooms or bats.[/b]
That is the mod, working as intended. His scene plays once per playthrough; from the second loop on, walking into the farm cave gives you the choice directly instead of replaying a cutscene you have already watched. The mushrooms-or-bats decision is re-offered every loop because the rewind clears it.

[b]The Traveling Cart only has one item.[/b]
Also intended. Joja is squeezing the merchant's suppliers, and the Cart Stall upgrades in the upgrade menu add slots back. If you would rather have the full cart, turn off LimitTravelingCartStock in the config.

[b]I did the Egg Hunt and now Lewis will not let me do it again today.[/b]
Since 0.14.1, a festival's main event runs once per day. Festivals in this mod do not end your day, so you can walk out and back in - which used to restart the whole festival and let the hunt be repeated for the prize. The stalls, the shop and everyone at the festival still work on a repeat visit. A new loop is a clean slate: as far as the valley is concerned the festival has not happened yet, so you get to do it again.

[b]A bundle is asking for silver or gold on something that cannot have a quality.[/b]
That was a bug and it is fixed. Quality is only ever asked for on things the game itself gives quality to (crop harvests, rod-caught fish, spawned forage). Existing boards pick the change up at the next reset.

[b]A weekly goal ticked off without me donating anything.[/b]
Fixed in 0.14.0. Finishing a bundle that only needs some of its listed items used to mark the rest as filled, which credited goals you never handed in. A goal now waits for the real donation.

[b]I bought Keep Bus Unlocked and the Vault bundles are still on the board.[/b]
Intended. The gift keeps the bus and the desert open from day 1; the Vault bundles are still part of restoring the Center, still have to be paid, and still earn JP. Completing them again does not replay the repair scene. Every Gift of the Junimos works this way.

[b]The skill level I bought at the statue was gone after the rewind.[/b]
Intended. Crash Course levels are temporary: they last the loop, never reach level 10, and cannot be kept. Only levels you earn open the Keep Level rows on a Fail night.

[b]Elevator Pass says "Enter the mine first", or a weather boost says "Not now".[/b]
Both intended. The pass extends the elevator from wherever it already reaches, so it needs one trip into the mine first. Rain Dance and Storm Call are refused on day 28 and the day before a festival, because the game forces sunshine on those mornings and the JP would be wasted.

[b]My enchanted sword lost its enchantments in the Junimo Stash.[/b]
Fixed since 0.16.7. Tools and weapons in the stash keep their enchantments, forged gems, bait and tackle across the rewind.

Anything not on this list, please do report - the bugs tab on Nexus is read.

[size=5][b]Limitations[/b][/size]
[list]
[*][b]PC only.[/b] No Android port yet.[/*]
[*][b]Other mods are not officially supported.[/b] TLY Custom boards ask only for vanilla items unless you turn on Allow mod items in custom bundles (off on new games; saves from before 0.19.4 start with it on), so by default other mods' items are left out and the balance holds. Normal or Remixed with other mods (including other bundle mods) is allowed, but the bundles may not reshuffle each loop and may ask for items you can't get. If something goes wrong with a specific mod, report it and I will take a look.[/*]
[*][b]Farm types are balanced as a set, not individually.[/b] The bundle asks are sized from Standard farm yields. Each other type trades one thing for another (Riverland and Beach: more fish, less field; Forest: more forage; Hilltop: more ore; Wilderness: more monsters; Meadowlands: easier animals), so the year is a little easier in some bundles and a little harder in others. Beach farm's no-sprinklers rule makes its crop bundles a real step harder. Custom farm maps that replace a vanilla slot load fine but are untested for balance.[/*]
[*][b]Start on a new save.[/b] A run can only begin from a new game; other saves load normally and are left untouched.[/*]
[*]Multiplayer is untested.[/*]
[/list][line]

[size=5][b]Giving feedback[/b][/size]
What helps most right now:
[list=1]
[*][b]Difficulty[/b]: do the seasonal minimums feel fair? Too punishing, too easy? Which season wall hit hardest?[/*]
[*][b]Pricing[/b]: are JP earnings and upgrade costs well-balanced? What did you save for first, and did it feel worth it?[/*]
[*][b]Pacing[/b]: how many loops before the run "clicked"? Did the carryover make later loops feel meaningfully stronger?[/*]
[*][b]Bugs / crashes[/b]: include your [font=Courier New]SMAPI-latest.txt[/font] ([font=Courier New]Stardew Valley/ErrorLogs/[/font]).[/*]
[/list][line]

[size=5][b]Art wanted[/b][/size]
The mod leans on vanilla sprites for most things. If anyone would enjoy making some custom [b]sprite artwork[/b] (the shrine, the stash chest, icons), I'd genuinely love to accept it and credit you. Drop a note in the comments.

[i]Banner art by [b]cwybabiesucks[/b]. Book art by [b]supercam19[/b]. Thank you both![/i]

[line]

[size=5][b]Translations[/b][/size]
As of 0.11.60, every player-visible string in the mod lives in a JSON file ([font=Courier New]i18n/default.json[/font]) — the mod is fully translatable with no DLL edits or rebuilds. See [url=https://github.com/sonofskywalker3/TheLongestYear/blob/master/docs/TRANSLATING.md]TRANSLATING.md[/url] for how to add a language. If you translate it, let us know (Nexus DM or GitHub issue) and we'll link your work from the mod page.

[line]
